title: Sharded activations + prefetch strategy evaluation for MoE routing on long contexts
body:
Purpose:
Quick notes and intermediate findings from experiments looking at how different activation sharding layouts and KV/activation prefetch heuristics affect MoE routing performance across Llama / Mistral / Qwen families when serving long-context (>=8k) workloads. This doc is an engineer-facing scratchpad — lightweight traces, numbers, and actions to reproduce/triage.

Background / motivation:
- In production MoE workloads we see sporadic p99 spikes when a large fraction of the batch routes to a small set of hot experts. On long-context requests this is amplified by sporadic KV cache prefetching and cross-GPU transfers.
- Two knobs we explored: (1) how activations are sharded across devices/expert partitions (layout), and (2) when/how we prefetch KV/activation blocks for upcoming tokens (prefetch strategy).
- Goal: reduce tail latency while keeping throughput and memory within Dedicated constraints (A100-80GB pools).

Cluster & test harness (short):
- Hardware: 4x A100-80GB (DGX-style), NVLink enabled. Also small-run on A10x8 (cloud).
- Models: Llama-2-70B-ish family trimmed to serve MoE variants (simulated experts), Mistral-Base-MoE-48E, Qwen-14B-MoE-64E (internal forks).
- MoE config: topk=2 gating, capacity_factor=1.0 default, expert_count 48/64 depending on model.
- Sequence lengths tested: 512, 2048, 8192, 32768 (where model supports).
- Batch shapes: interactive-style (1-4) and batched throughput (16/32).
- Measurements: token throughput, tail latency p50/p95/p99, peak GPU memory, cudaMalloc count, kernel launch counts, PCIe/NVLink bytes (driver counters), profiler traces (nsighttm).

Shard layouts evaluated:
- contiguous-per-expert: each expert's activations live contiguously on a single GPU memory region. Simple and minimal scatter/gather work.
- interleaved-stride: activations interleaved across GPUs (stripe across experts). Improves memory balance but more scatter/gather kernels.
- tile-by-seq: tile activations by sequence segment (useful for very long contexts where later tokens touch different experts).

Prefetch strategies evaluated:
- eager-prefetch: prefetch next K token KV blocks for every request immediately after routing decision (K tuned).
- demand-prefetch: prefetch only when predicted routing heat > threshold (hot-expert watermark).
- batched-window: accumulate N requests then prefetch a window; trades latency for aggregated transfer efficiency.

Key micro-observations (experimental):
1) Memory / OOM behavior:
   - contiguous-per-expert had the lowest peak allocation and most deterministic allocator behavior (cudaMallocAsync calls low). On A100, this layout survived 32k context runs for Llama-ish models at batch=2.
   - interleaved-stride reduced peak per-GPU by ~18% in mixed expert-load cases, but increased transient allocations due to scatter+gather temp buffers; this triggered occasional OOMs on A10 runs (smaller RAM).

2) Latency / kernel patterns:
   - eager-prefetch reduced stall time during long streaming sequences: observed ~25% reduction in average per-token stall for seq=8192.
   - however, eager-prefetch increased p99 in several cases because it pushed memory pressure earlier in the pipeline and forced fallback copies (device->host->device) when NVLink congestion hit.
   - demand-prefetch (watermark=0.6 of expert-hotness) yielded the best p99/throughput tradeoff: kept eager-like stalls low for true hot-spikes but avoided prefetch churn for low-traffic tokens.

3) Routing interaction with attention implementation:
   - Mistral's chunked attention (four-way block) interacts poorly with early-prefetch: prefetching KV blocks that don't align with Mistral's chunk boundaries caused an extra copy + kernel split, adding ~15-22% kernel overhead for the attention block.
   - Llama-style attention (monolithic) benefited more consistently from prefetch. Qwen had intermediate behavior.

4) Scatter/gather kernel hotspots:
   - The gates and scatter kernels (internal names seen in traces: moe_router_kernel, gather_expert_outputs, scatter_to_expert) dominate p99 when topk>1 and load is skewed.
   - Interleaved sharding adds an additional scatter stage which increases kernel launch count by 1.6x on average, and increases CPU dispatch latency (host-device sync) in our current runtime.

5) NVLink vs PCIe tradeoffs:
   - When NVLink is available and not saturated, inter-GPU prefetch transfers are ~3x faster (expected). However, if many concurrent prefetches occur (eager), we see NVLink congestion that forces transfers to fallback over PCIe -> orders-of-magnitude increases in transfer time and p99 spikes.

Concrete numbers (representative sample):
- Qwen-14B-MoE-64E, seq=8192, batch=4, topk=2:
   - contiguous + demand-prefetch (watermark 0.6): throughput=18 tok/s per GPU, p95=120ms, p99=310ms, peak mem=65GB.
   - interleaved + eager-prefetch (K=4): throughput=21 tok/s per GPU, p95=130ms, p99=540ms, peak mem=76GB, kernel_launches +60%.
   - contiguous + eager-prefetch: throughput=19 tok/s, p95=115ms, p99=420ms.

Hypotheses / intuitive summaries:
- If memory headroom exists and NVLink is uncongested, eager-prefetch + interleaved sharding gives highest throughput but brittle p99. Good for best-effort batch jobs.
- For interactive, tail-sensitive workloads prefer contiguous sharding + demand-prefetch with conservative watermark (<0.7) and smaller K.
- Model-specific attention implementation matters: Mistral needs alignment-aware prefetch to avoid splitting attention kernels.

Short-term mitigations tried in runtime: 
- Implemented a watermark-based demand-prefetch flag (configurable) and saw immediate p99 improvements on our staging fleet.
- Added a gating heuristic that disables eager-prefetch when NVLink measured saturation > 60% (simple sentinel using perf counters).

Actionable next experiments (priority order):
- A/B sweep of watermark thresholds: 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 across models and seq lengths — measure p50/p95/p99 and OOM rates. (Ticket: JIRA-SERV-4721)
- Kernel fusion: explore fusing scatter + gather into single kernel to reduce launch overhead for interleaved layout. See PR branch: runtime/pull/611.
- Alignment-aware prefetch: implement prefetch granularity that matches model attention tile size for Mistral to avoid split kernels.
- Adaptive topk for tail-sensitive routes: temporarily reduce topk during hot spikes to limit scatter degree. Measure quality regression separately.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to quantify QoE impact for adaptive topk? Needs human eval or automated downstream metric.
- Can we push prefetch logic into GPU (kernel-driven prefetch) to avoid host dispatch storms? (research)
- Is there a workable hybrid allocation strategy (cudaMallocAsync + reserved pool) that avoids transient temp buffers for interleaved layout?

Repro steps (minimal):
1) Checkout branch runtime/pull/611 and the local benchmark harness.
2) Start 4x A100 instance pool; NVLink enabled recommended.
3) Run harness: ./bench_moe.sh --model qwen-14b-moe --seq 8192 --batch 4 --layout contiguous --prefetch demand --watermark 0.6 --trace nsight_out
4) Collect traces: nsight, nsys, and the runtime debug logs. Upload to CONFLUENCE-RT-2389 for centralized trace review.

Notes for SRE / Deployment:
- Defaulting eager-prefetch in staging caused two OOM incidents on older fleet nodes with slower NVLink backplanes; reverted to demand-prefetch.
- Add telemetry for: (a) NVLink saturation flag, (b) per-request prefetch bytes, (c) scatter kernel time per-request. These three signals are most predictive of imminent p99 blowups.

References and quick links:
- CONFLUENCE-RT-2389 (perf traces + gantt of experiments)
- JIRA-SERV-4721 (sweep tasks + experiment tracker)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/611 (fusion/proof-of-concept kernels)
- Slack: #moe-perf thread 1693204820 (ops notes)

Bottom line (engineer TL;DR):
- Don’t enable eager-prefetch universally. Use demand-prefetch with watermark around 0.5-0.7 for latency-sensitive interactive workloads.
- Prefer contiguous-per-expert sharding for predictable mem usage and tail stability; interleaved can help throughput if you accept higher p99 and invest in kernel fusion and allocator tuning.

Next owner: Ravi Patel to run watermark sweep (see JIRA-SERV-4721). Diego to prototype a fused scatter/gather kernel in branch runtime/pull/611. Margaret to draft a short runbook for SRE describing when to flip prefetch mode in staging/fleet.

(rough notes end)
